page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.12xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by a 24-core, 48-vCPU Intel Xeon 8252C processor capable of reaching clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz, the system features a dedicated CPU allocation with two threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 24 MB L3 cache, complemented by instruction support for AVX-512, AVX512 VNNI, AES, and FMA.

Memory capacity is the defining specification of the instance, provisioning 1,536 GB of 3 GHz DDR4 RAM, resulting in an extreme memory-to-vCPU allocation of 32 GB per thread. Network throughput is provisioned at a 100 Gbps baseline. The instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent and temporary block storage operations must be configured over external network-attached services such as Amazon EBS. There are no onboard graphics processing units or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark results reflect high throughput across memory and compute-intensive operations. The instance achieved strong top-quartile performance in uncached memory bandwidth, delivering 209.78 GB/sec in 256 MB reads and 98.02 GB/sec in writes, alongside a strong PassMark memory score of 2,902.21. Compute benchmarks show solid execution, recording 49,124.89 in PassMark CPU tests and 40,125.0 in Clang software compilation. Conversely, LLM text generation metrics sit in the lower quartile, yielding 46.23 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models and 7.82 tokens/sec on 7B models, illustrating the limits of purely CPU-bound autoregressive text generation.

The hardware configuration provides high density for memory-bound applications without the overhead of physical cluster management. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local non-volatile storage, which places I/O demands entirely on network infrastructure. The x2iezn.12xlarge is technically best matched for large-scale in-memory databases, SAP HANA deployments, real-time analytics engines, and enterprise electronic design automation workloads requiring substantial RAM alongside high single-thread clock rates.

Network connectivity features a 100 Gbps baseline. The instance contains zero bundled local NVMe storage and no GPU accelerators, depending entirely on network-attached storage for disk operations.
